title: Covering a cake in marzipan
subtitle: the traditional first layer before royal icing or fondant
excerpt: Marzipan covering seals a fruit cake before royal icing or sugarpaste goes on, filling surface irregularities and providing a firm, smooth base. The cake is brushed with apricot jam first to help the marzipan adhere. Most fruit cakes need 500 g to 750 g of marzipan to cover a 20 to 23 cm round.
sourceNotes: Mrs Beeton, Book of Household Management (1861), Project Gutenberg #10136, covering method for Christmas cake. The apricot glaze adhesion step is documented in British cake-decorating manuals from the 1950s onward.

glossaryTerms.definition: Apricot jam warmed with a little water and sieved smooth, used to brush onto a fruit cake before marzipan covering to act as an adhesive.
A firm paste made from ground almonds and sugar, rolled and draped over a cake to provide a smooth base for icing.

content.text: fills any surface dips, seals in the fruit, and gives royal icing or fondant a firm, level base to grip. The cake is brushed first with warmed
, which helps the marzipan adhere. Once on, the marzipan needs 24 hours to dry before icing is applied.
For a 20 cm round cake, use 500 g of marzipan. For a 23 cm round, 700 g. For a 25 cm round or a deep 23 cm tin, 1 kg. Roll it on a surface lightly dusted with icing sugar to stop it sticking.
Warm 3 to 4 tablespoons of apricot jam with a splash of water in a small pan until fluid. Push through a sieve to remove any fruit pieces and set aside to cool slightly.
Place the cake flat-side-down on a board. Brush the top and sides thoroughly with the warm glaze. Let it sit for 5 minutes to become slightly tacky.

Knead the marzipan briefly to soften it. Roll it out on a surface lightly dusted with icing sugar to a circle about 5 mm thick. For a 20 cm cake, roll to about 33 cm in diameter to cover the top and sides in one piece.

Lift the marzipan over the rolling pin and drape it centrally over the top of the cake. Smooth the top with the palm of your hand, then work the sides down using smooth downward strokes, easing out pleats as you go.
Trim the excess from the base of the cake with a sharp knife held flush with the board. Press the cut edge gently against the side to seal.
Smooth the sides with a cake smoother or the flat of your hand, using circular motions. Leave to dry for 24 hours in a cool, dry room before applying any icing.

attrs.problem: Marzipan tearing as it is draped over the cake
attrs.avoid: Avoid rolling marzipan too thin; less than 4 mm tears easily.
attrs.fix: Knead any tears closed, smooth over with a little icing sugar on your fingertip, and re-drape.

attrs.problem: Pleats at the sides that will not smooth out
attrs.avoid: Avoid pulling the marzipan tightly downward; ease it into the sides gradually.
attrs.fix: Cut a pleat with a sharp knife, overlap the edges slightly, and press to seal.
